title: Work & study
goal: Talk about jobs, school and university, and say what you can, can't, must and have to do.
intro: 'What do you do?' — **توهان ڇا ڪندا آهيو؟** — is one of the first questions you'll be asked. In this unit you'll learn job and study words and two essential verb patterns: **سگهڻ** for ability ('can') and the **-ṇo آهي / -ṇo پوندو** construction for obligation ('have to').

vocab.note: f. نوڪري ڪرڻ = to have a job, work.
m. Much of rural Sindh lives by farming.
f. موڪل وٺڻ = to take leave.
f. محنت ڪرڻ = to work hard.
Used after another verb: ڪري سگهان ٿو = I can do.

phrases.en: What do you do (for a living)?

phrases.native: مان استاد آهيان، هڪ اسڪول ۾ پڙهايان ٿو.
phrases.roman: māṃ ustādu āhiyāṃ, hika iskūla meṃ paṛhāyāṃ tho.
phrases.en: I'm a teacher; I teach at a school. (man)

phrases.roman: māṃ sindha yūnivarsiṭīa meṃ paṛhāṃ thī.

phrases.native: هو هاري آهي، ڪڻڪ ۽ ڪپهه پوکي ٿو.
phrases.roman: hū hārī āhe, kaṇaka ai kapaha pokhe tho.
phrases.en: He's a farmer; he grows wheat and cotton.

phrases.native: ڇا توهان ڪمپيوٽر هلائي سگهو ٿا؟
phrases.roman: chhā tavhāṃ kampyūṭaru halāe sagho thā?

phrases.native: مان سنڌي پڙهي سگهان ٿو، پر لکي نٿو سگهان.
phrases.roman: māṃ sindhī paṛhī saghāṃ tho, para likhī natho saghāṃ.
phrases.en: I can read Sindhi but I can't write it. (man)

phrases.native: مون کي سڀاڻي جلدي آفيس وڃڻو آهي.
phrases.roman: moṃ khe subhāṇe jaldī āfīsa vañaṇo āhe.
phrases.en: I have to go to the office early tomorrow.

phrases.native: اسان کي امتحان لاءِ محنت ڪرڻي پوندي.
phrases.roman: asāṃ khe imtihāna lāi mehnata karaṇī pavandī.
phrases.en: We'll have to work hard for the exam.

phrases.native: مون کي ڪالهه دير تائين ڪم ڪرڻو پيو.
phrases.roman: moṃ khe kālha dera tāīṃ kamu karaṇo peyo.
phrases.en: I had to work late yesterday.

grammar.title: Ability: verb + سگهڻ 'can'
grammar.body:
'Can' is the verb **سگهڻ** (saghaṇu). The main verb comes first in a linking form ending in **-ī / -e** (the stem + ي), then سگهڻ carries the tense and person:

مان ڳالهائي سگهان ٿو — I can speak (man)
توهان اچي سگهو ٿا؟ — can you come?
هوءَ پڙهي سگهي ٿي — she can read

Negative: **نٿو سگهان** etc. — مان اچي نٿو سگهان 'I can't come'. Past: سگهيس / نه سگهيس 'I could / couldn't' (more in Unit 16).

For skills learned ('know how to'), Sindhi also uses **اچڻ** 'to come' with کي: مون کي سنڌي اچي ٿي 'Sindhi comes to me' = I know Sindhi; هن کي ترڻ اچي ٿو 'he knows how to swim'.

examples.native: ڇا توهان سڀاڻي اچي سگهو ٿا؟
examples.roman: chhā tavhāṃ subhāṇe achī sagho thā?

examples.native: مون کي ٿوري سنڌي اچي ٿي.
examples.roman: moṃ khe thorī sindhī ache thī.

grammar.title: Obligation: 'have to' with -ṇo آهي / پوندو / پيو
grammar.body:
To say **'have to'**, Sindhi uses the person + **کي**, then the infinitive turned into an adjective ending **-ṇo**, then a form of 'to be' or 'to fall':

**مون کي وڃڻو آهي** — I have to go (it's on my agenda)
**مون کي وڃڻو پوندو** — I'll have to go (unavoidable, future)
**مون کي وڃڻو پيو** — I had to go (past)

If the verb has a **feminine object**, the -ṇo form agrees with it: مون کي **چٺي لکڻي** آهي 'I have to write a letter' (چٺي f), اسان کي **محنت ڪرڻي** پوندي 'we'll have to work hard' (محنت f).

For 'must / should' (advice or moral obligation) use infinitive + **گهرجي** (Unit 9). For 'it's necessary that…' use **ضروري آهي ته …**.

examples.native: مون کي هاڻي گهر وڃڻو آهي.
examples.roman: moṃ khe hāṇe ghara vañaṇo āhe.
examples.en: I have to go home now.

examples.native: هن کي ڇنڇر تي به ڪم ڪرڻو پوي ٿو.
examples.roman: hun khe chhanchhara te bi kamu karaṇo pave tho.
examples.en: He/She has to work on Saturdays too.
You'll have to fill in a form.

examples.roman: asāṃ khe ṭreni meṃ bīhaṇo peyo.
examples.en: We had to stand on the train.

examples.native: ضروري آهي ته توهان وقت تي اچو.
examples.roman: zarūrī āhe ta tavhāṃ vaqta te acho.
examples.en: It's important that you come on time.

dialogue.title: A new job
dialogue.setting: Bilawal meets his old school friend Zubair in a café in Karachi.

lines.speaker: Zubair
lines.native: بلاول! ڪيترن سالن کان پوءِ! اڄڪلهه ڇا پيو ڪرين؟
lines.roman: Bilāval! ketiran sālan khāṃ poi! aʄkalha chhā peyo kareṃ?
lines.en: Bilawal! After so many years! What are you up to these days?

lines.speaker: Bilawal
lines.native: مان هڪ بئنڪ ۾ نوڪري ڪريان ٿو. ۽ تون؟
lines.roman: māṃ hika bainka meṃ nokirī karyāṃ tho. ai tūṃ?
lines.en: I work in a bank. And you?

lines.speaker: Zubair
lines.native: مان انجنيئر آهيان، پر هاڻي ٻي نوڪري ڳولي رهيو آهيان.
lines.roman: māṃ injinīru āhiyāṃ, para hāṇe ɓī nokirī ɠole rahyo āhiyāṃ.
lines.en: I'm an engineer, but I'm looking for another job now.

lines.speaker: Zubair
lines.native: پگهار ٺيڪ آهي، پر روز ٻارهن ڪلاڪ ڪم ڪرڻو پوي ٿو.
lines.roman: pagāra ṭhīku āhe, para roz ɓārahaṃ kalāka kamu karaṇo pave tho.
lines.en: The salary's fine, but I have to work twelve hours every day.

lines.speaker: Bilawal
lines.native: ٻارهن ڪلاڪ! پوءِ ٻارن سان وقت ڪيئن ٿو گذارين؟
lines.roman: ɓārahaṃ kalāka! poi ɓāran sāṃ vaqtu kīeṃ tho guzāreṃ?
lines.en: Twelve hours! Then how do you spend time with the kids?

lines.speaker: Zubair
lines.native: بلڪل. ڇا تنهنجي بئنڪ ۾ ڪا جاءِ خالي آهي؟
lines.roman: bilkul. chhā tunhinjī bainka meṃ kā jāi xālī āhe?
lines.en: Exactly. Is there a vacancy at your bank?

lines.speaker: Bilawal
lines.native: مان پڇي سگهان ٿو. تو کي پنهنجي سي وي موڪلڻي پوندي.
lines.roman: māṃ puchhī saghāṃ tho. to khe panhinjī sī vī moklaṇī pavandī.
lines.en: I can ask. You'll have to send your CV.

lines.speaker: Zubair
lines.en: I'll send it today itself. Thanks, mate!

culture: Sindh's economy combines a huge port city (Karachi, Pakistan's commercial capital) with a rural heartland of farming — wheat, rice, cotton, sugarcane, bananas and mangoes — where the relationship between the هاري (tenant farmer) and the landowner (زميندار، وڏيرو) has long shaped society and politics. **Sindh University** at Jamshoro (founded 1947) is one of Pakistan's oldest universities, and Sindhi is a compulsory school subject in the province. Teachers are deeply respected: a former teacher remains 'ustād' or 'sāīṃ' for life.
